comment: Hand-authored micro-polish of the CASCO (EnvPolish). The district scene is generated, so every local correction lives here and survives a rebuild. 'plots': BuildingSpec field overrides by building id ('K4_0_2'). 'ops': object corrections on the built district, found by exact module name within r metres of a world point (near = x,y,z as built): remove | move (to = [x,z] on the ground or [x,y,z], or by = [dx,dy,dz]; optional yaw, scale) | place (module, at = [x,z] or [x,y,z], yaw, scale). Every entry says its inspection unit (Docs/evidence/WP-PROD-ENV-01/micro-polish/UNITS.md) and why, and marks its class: TECH (technical), SEM (makes no sense to a person). | night2-D7: removed 6 orphan ops whose targets no longer exist after the phase-3 rebuild (chair Cimavilla, 3 chalkboards, Espina_Nodo barrel, Calle_Alta_O bench); the Pasarela barrel op still hits and stays.

K11_0_1.why: The portal sill sat 0.59 m below the paving in front of it: the building stands on the lowest ground of its plot on an 8 % lane and the door is at the uphill end. Lifted to the door's level; its stone base grows by the same amount.

K14_3_6.why: Same case on San Pedro: the portal sill sat 0.53 m below the paving in front of it.

K15_5_1.why: K15_5_1 and K14_0_0 (both Solana lanes) were built with the identical ground floor D,P,R: two cloned frontages a street apart. K15_5_1's stone ground floor already reads as a work yard; pinned to a taller (timber gate) so the two differ at a glance.

K6_11_2.why: River frontage 6.5 m with no opening on any floor (audit BLANK_WALL): the third bay column was plain on all four floors. A small window on the first floor gives the quay wall a lived front like its neighbours. Fase 3: a grey dressed stone floor-line band (the quay course) crosses the party seam with K6_11_3, so the two renders read as one house split by a course, not two buildings stitched together.

K6_11_3.why: River frontage 6.5 m with no opening on any floor (audit BLANK_WALL, same run as K6_11_2): its first two bays were plain on both floors. A small window on the upper floor continues the staggered rhythm of the row. Fase 3: the two new first-floor windows sat a hand higher than the sill line of the neighbouring quay windows (painted ashlar surrounds, sill ~1.05, against the kit line ~0.94); surrounds off drops them onto the neighbour line, and the shared grey dressed floor-line band ties the seam.

K2_13_0.why: The portal opened onto paving 1.4 m beyond the street edge, under the broken balustrade of the promenade (audit DOOR_NOWHERE, owner-confirmed on Ribera fwd_03): a door that leads nowhere. The bay becomes a small window; the house is entered from the other side.

K13_5_0.why: The portal opened straight onto bare ground and a slope, no pavement in front of it (audit DOOR_NOWHERE, owner-confirmed on Calle_Alta_Salida fwd_01). The bay becomes a small window beside the shop; the way in is the shop door.

ops.why: K6_10_1 (river house): the audit flagged the facade as FLAT_FACADE — nothing stands out more than 12 cm. An iron balconera under the west upper-floor window, like its neighbour houses on the quay.

K0_6_0 (river house, reappeared after the phase-3 full rebuild): FLAT_FACADE — nothing stands out from the front. An iron balconera under the first-floor shuttered window, the quay language of K6_10_1 two doors along.

K8_12_2 (river house, reappeared after the phase-3 full rebuild): FLAT_FACADE — the Hueso row behind the K6_11 gap reads as one flat plane. An iron balconera under its stacked first/second-floor window axis.
Pasarela south landing: a barrel stood 0.30 m sunk into the paving beside the steps (its ground sample caught the slope down to the water). Lifted back onto the paving.
